mainTopic: Whether גיד הנשה applies to a non-kosher animal, and how רבי יהודה's view fits with אין איסור חל על איסור
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion about a forbidden piece cooked in a pot. It uses the rule of מין ומינו ודבר אחר: the same kind of food is ignored, and only the different kind can cancel the forbidden piece. Then a new משנה teaches that גיד הנשה applies only to a kosher animal, while רבי יהודה says it applies to a non-kosher animal too. רבי יהודה's proof is that בני יעקב were already forbidden the גיד when non-kosher animals were still permitted to them. The חכמים answer that the איסור was really given at סיני. The גמרא then asks how רבי יהודה can hold this, since a ברייתא shows he holds אין איסור חל על איסור. The גמרא first suggests that both איסורים start together in the שליל, but a משנה about a נזיר shows the non-kosher איסור comes first. The final answer is that the גיד הנשה איסור takes effect anyway because it also applies to בני נח, and רבי יהודה's own wording in the משנה supports this. The amud ends as the גמרא returns to study the ברייתא about two sets of lashes, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even without removing the piece, it is a mixture of same-kind and other-kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even if the forbidden piece was not removed first, the case counts as מין ומינו ודבר אחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say he did not remove the forbidden piece first. It is still a case of one kind of food mixed with its own kind and with something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving its final answer to the earlier question about a forbidden piece cooked in a pot. It says we do not need the case where the piece was taken out first, because the mixture is of a special type.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא suggested the ruling only fits if the forbidden piece was removed first. Now it says the ruling works even if the piece stayed in. The pot holds the forbidden piece, other pieces of the same kind, and also broth and spices, which are a different kind.

keyTerms.meaning: You may even say; a way of answering that widens the case
He removed it first, before the rest was cooked or added
A forbidden food mixed with its own kind and also with a different kind of food

phrases.english: You may even say he did not first remove it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the forbidden piece of meat or fish from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: it is a case of a type with its own type and something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous part of the daf about the cooked forbidden piece.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the case into a known category, so the earlier limit on the case is not needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling only works if the forbidden piece was removed first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if it was not removed, the ruling stands because the mixture is מין ומינו ודבר אחר.

steps.title: The rule: ignore the same kind, and only the other kind can cancel it
steps.stepSummary: In a mixture of מין ומינו ודבר אחר, you treat the same kind as if it is not there. Only the different kind can cancel the forbidden food, if there is enough of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any mixture of a food with its own kind and with something else, take away its own kind as if it is not there. The food that is not its kind, if there is more of it, cancels the forbidden food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the general rule behind the answer in Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same-kind food does not help cancel the forbidden food here. Only the different-kind food (the broth and spices) counts toward the amount needed for ביטול. If the forbidden flavor already spread into the other same-kind pieces, the different-kind food must be enough to cancel all of them, and it may not be.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove its own kind as though it were not there
Food that is not of the same kind
Is more than it, enough to outweigh it
Cancels it (ביטול), so the mixture becomes permitted

steps.whatToRemember: In מין ומינו ודבר אחר, only the different kind of food counts toward cancelling the forbidden food. The same kind is ignored.

phrases.english: And in any case of a type with its own type and something else –
remove its own type as though it is not there,
and what is not its type, if it is greater than it, nullifies it.
phrases.notes: "Greater" here means enough to cancel it, which the earlier discussion measured as sixty times as much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle that makes the answer in Step 1 work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a mixture of מין ומינו ודבר אחר, the same kind is ignored, and only the different kind can cancel the forbidden food.

steps.title: New משנה: does גיד הנשה apply to a non-kosher animal?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the איסור of גיד הנשה applies only to a kosher animal. רבי יהודה says it applies to a non-kosher animal too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The איסור of גיד הנשה applies to a kosher animal and not to a non-kosher animal. רבי יהודה says: even to a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a מחלוקת about whether the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, a non-kosher animal is forbidden anyway, so no separate גיד הנשה prohibition applies to it. רבי יהודה holds that its גיד carries its own גיד הנשה prohibition as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Applies; is in effect
A kosher animal
A non-kosher animal
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Everyone agrees a non-kosher animal is forbidden to eat. The argument is only whether its גיד also carries the extra גיד הנשה prohibition.

phrases.english: MISHNA: It applies to a kosher animal,
phrases.notes: "It" is the איסור of eating the גיד הנשה, which is the subject of this פרק.

phrases.english: and does not apply to a non-kosher animal.
Rabbi Yehuda says: Even to a non-kosher animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: גיד הנשה applies only to a kosher animal. רבי יהודה: it applies to a non-kosher animal too.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's proof from the sons of יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that גיד הנשה was forbidden to the sons of יעקב at a time when non-kosher animals were still permitted to them. So the איסור covered every animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Wasn't גיד הנשה forbidden from the time of the sons of יעקב, while a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a proof for his opinion from the time of the אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back then, non-kosher animals were permitted, so the גיד הנשה prohibition must have applied to them too. A law that once covered non-kosher animals still covers them, even after the whole animal became forbidden at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so...? (introduces a strong proof)
The sons of יעקב
The sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to eat
And still; while at that time

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: But isn't it so that
from the sons of Jacob the sciatic nerve was forbidden,
while a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב נֶאֱסַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי יהודה's opinion in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that גיד הנשה applies to a non-kosher animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in בראשית shows גיד הנשה was forbidden to the sons of יעקב, back when non-kosher animals were permitted.

steps.title: The חכמים: it was given at סיני, just written in that place
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the איסור of גיד הנשה was really given at סיני. The תורה only wrote it in the story of יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It was said at סיני, but it was written in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push away רבי יהודה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's proof depends on the איסור starting in יעקב's time. The חכמים say it actually began at סיני, when non-kosher animals were already forbidden. So it never covered non-kosher animals. The פסוק appears in the story of יעקב only because that is where the event happened.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said, meaning commanded, at סיני
It was written in its place, in the story where the event took place

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת depends on when the איסור began. If it began with יעקב, it covered all animals. If it began at סיני, it covered only kosher ones.

phrases.english: They said to him: It was stated at Sinai,
but it was written in its place.
phrases.notes: "Its place" means the story of יעקב fighting the מלאך, where the injury to the גיד happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof from Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the time of the sons of יעקב, not רבי יהודה's ruling itself directly
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the איסור began with יעקב, but it actually began at סיני.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really hold that one איסור takes effect on another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה holds איסור חל על איסור, since his view adds the גיד הנשה prohibition onto an animal that is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that a prohibition takes effect on top of another prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge. It points out that רבי יהודה's view seems to need איסור חל על איסור, and it is about to show that he holds the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal is already forbidden as טמאה. If its גיד is also forbidden as גיד הנשה, then a second איסור has taken effect on something already forbidden. The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really accepts this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
And does he hold...? (questions someone's opinion)
A prohibition takes effect on something that is already prohibited

steps.whyThisMatters: איסור חל על איסור is a basic idea across ש״ס. The גמרא will test whether רבי יהודה is consistent with it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold
that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's opinion in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that גיד הנשה applies to a non-kosher animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling requires איסור חל על איסור, but elsewhere he seems to reject that idea.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a non-kosher bird's carcass
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא from רבי יהודה about whether a non-kosher bird's carcass makes clothing טמא when swallowed. This will support the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: One might think the carcass of a non-kosher bird makes clothing impure when it is in the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its challenge. The ברייתא is only starting here, and the next step completes its point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with "one might think," which means רבי יהודה is about to reject this idea. Watch for his reason, because it will show how he views איסור חל על איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (an idea that will be rejected)
The carcass of a non-kosher bird
Makes clothing טמא
The throat, at the moment of swallowing

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One might have thought that the carcass of a non-kosher bird
renders garments impure when in the throat?
phrases.notes: "One might have thought" means he is comparing it to a kosher bird's carcass, which does make clothes טמא when swallowed. He will reject the comparison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that backs up the challenge in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהודה does not hold איסור חל על איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה discusses the טומאה of a non-kosher bird's carcass. Its conclusion comes in Step 8.

steps.title: The verse excludes a non-kosher bird from carcass טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by reading the פסוק to say that only a bird forbidden as נבלה makes a person טמא. A non-kosher bird, which is already forbidden as טמאה, is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'A carcass or a torn animal he shall not eat, to become impure through it.' This means a bird that is forbidden because of 'do not eat a carcass.' It leaves out a bird that is not forbidden because of 'do not eat a carcass,' but because of 'do not eat a non-kosher animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא of רבי יהודה. It shows that a non-kosher bird's carcass does not make a person טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the איסור of נבלה never takes hold on a non-kosher bird, because that bird is already forbidden as טמאה. This shows he holds אין איסור חל על איסור. That makes the question from step 6 stronger: how can the איסור of גיד הנשה take hold on a non-kosher animal, which is already forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach
An animal or bird that died without proper שחיטה
An animal or bird with a fatal injury or defect
'Do not eat', the wording of a negative command
A non-kosher species
A second prohibition does not take hold on something already forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proof that רבי יהודה holds אין איסור חל על איסור. The rest of the sugya has to explain how his view on גיד הנשה fits with that rule.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"A carcass or a torn animal he shall not eat
to become impure through it".
This means one whose prohibition is because of "do not eat a carcass".
This leaves out one whose prohibition is not
because of "do not eat a carcass"
but because of "do not eat a non-kosher one".
phrases.notes: In other words, a non-kosher bird is already forbidden for a different reason, so the carcass rule never reaches it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 7
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds אין איסור חל על איסור

steps.title: Maybe the nerve has no taste, so only one prohibition applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out: perhaps רבי יהודה holds that nerves have no taste. Then in a non-kosher animal only the גיד איסור applies, and the non-kosher איסור does not apply to the nerve at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that he holds nerves do not give flavor, then in a non-kosher animal too the nerve prohibition is there, but the non-kosher prohibition is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense for רבי יהודה. Since it is only offered so it can be tested, this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nerve has no taste, it is not real food, so the איסור of a non-kosher animal does not cover it. Then the גיד הנשה איסור would not be landing on anything already forbidden. In that case there is no clash with אין איסור חל על איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggested answer)
Nerves or sinews
Gives taste, meaning it counts as food

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. It is a suggestion that gets rejected in the very next step.

phrases.english: And if you would say
he holds that nerves do not give flavor,
then in a non-kosher animal as well
there is the prohibition of the nerve,
but the prohibition of non-kosher is not there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a defense against the challenge strengthened in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the overlap: the non-kosher איסור never covers a tasteless nerve
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both איסורים would overlap on the nerve, which רבי יהודה should not allow
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the גיד איסור applies, so there is no overlap

steps.title: רבי יהודה gives two sets of lashes, so the nerve must have taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. A ברייתא says רבי יהודה makes someone who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal liable twice, so the non-kosher איסור does apply to the nerve.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יהודה really hold that nerves do not give flavor? Isn't it taught: one who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal, רבי יהודה makes him liable twice, and רבי שמעון exempts him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 9 by quoting a ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's real view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sets of lashes mean both the גיד איסור and the non-kosher איסור apply to the same nerve. That only makes sense if the nerve has taste and counts as food. So the way out is gone, and the clash with אין איסור חל על איסור comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds him liable twice (two sets of lashes)
Exempts

phrases.english: But does רבי יהודה hold
that nerves do not give flavor?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One who eats the גיד הנשה
of a non-kosher animal:
רבי יהודה holds him liable twice,
phrases.notes: Once for the nerve and once for eating from a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: and רבי שמעון exempts him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֵין בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יהודה holds nerves have no taste
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sets of lashes prove both איסורים apply to the nerve, so it must count as food

steps.title: Both prohibitions start together in the unborn calf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the nerve does have taste. But רבי יהודה holds גיד הנשה applies to an unborn calf, so the nerve איסור and the non-kosher איסור begin at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he holds nerves do give flavor. He also holds the איסור applies to a fetus, so the nerve prohibition and the non-kosher prohibition come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how רבי יהודה can give two sets of lashes and still hold אין איסור חל על איסור. This answer is challenged in Steps 12 and 14, and its timing claim is rejected in Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule אין איסור חל על איסור only blocks a second איסור that comes after the first one. Since the גיד הנשה איסור already applies while the animal is a שליל, both איסורים start at once. Neither one lands on top of the other, so both apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Really (keeps the original idea and explains it another way)
An unborn calf still inside its mother
Together, at the same time

steps.whatToRemember: This answer depends on two claims: that רבי יהודה applies גיד הנשה to a שליל, and that both איסורים start at the same moment. The next steps test each claim, and the second one is rejected in Step 15.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key limit of אין איסור חל על איסור: it does not block two איסורים that start at the same moment.

phrases.english: Really, he holds
that nerves do give flavor,
and he holds that it applies to a fetus,
phrases.notes: "It" means the איסור of גיד הנשה, which already applies while the calf is still in its mother.

phrases.english: so the prohibition of the nerve and the prohibition of non-kosher
come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם, קָסָבַר יֵשׁ בְּגִידִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 with a new explanation of the question in step 6. Steps 12-15 then challenge this explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: both איסורים start at the same moment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גיד איסור would land on an animal already forbidden as non-kosher
steps.terutzMaskana: In the שליל both איסורים begin together, so both apply and there are two sets of lashes

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really apply גיד הנשה to a fetus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer with a משנה where רבי יהודה says גיד הנשה does not apply to a שליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say that רבי יהודה holds גיד הנשה applies to a fetus? But a משנה says the תנא קמא holds it applies to a fetus, while רבי יהודה says it does not apply, and the fetus's fat is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 11. It quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה says the very opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 needed רבי יהודה to hold that גיד הנשה applies to an unborn calf, so that both איסורים could start together. But the משנה shows רבי יהודה is the one who says it does NOT apply to a שליל. So the answer seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: An unborn calf, a fetus still inside its mother
Applies (the law is in force)
Its forbidden fat (חלב)
Can you say?

phrases.english: And can you really say
that it applies to a fetus?
phrases.notes: "It" is the גיד הנשה איסור. Step 11 said רבי יהודה holds this.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
It applies to a fetus;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it does not apply to a fetus,
and its fat is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise of the answer in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds גיד הנשה applies to a שליל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה directly quotes רבי יהודה saying גיד הנשה does not apply to a שליל, the opposite of what Step 11 needed

steps.title: רבי יהודה exempts a fetus only in a kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's exemption of the שליל comes from a פסוק about kosher animals, so in a non-kosher animal גיד הנשה does apply to the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule is only about a kosher animal, because the תורה says 'every animal... inside the animal you may eat.' But in a non-kosher animal, גיד הנשה does apply to the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רבי יהודה's rule. The fetus is exempt only in a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ״כֹּל בַּבְּהֵמָה תֹּאכֵלוּ״ teaches that what is inside a kosher animal may be eaten along with it. That reason only works for an animal you are allowed to eat. So in a non-kosher animal the fetus's גיד is still forbidden, and the answer in Step 11 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only (limits the scope of a statement)
A kosher species of animal
A non-kosher species of animal
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: This applies only to a kosher animal,
because the Merciful One said:
"Every... among the animals you may eat,"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:6. בַּבְּהֵמָה can also mean "inside the animal," so what is inside a kosher animal may be eaten too.

phrases.english: but in a non-kosher animal it applies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 by narrowing רבי יהודה's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה exempts every fetus from גיד הנשה
steps.terutzMaskana: He exempts only the fetus of a kosher animal, because of the פסוק. In a non-kosher animal the fetus's גיד is forbidden.

steps.title: Do both איסורים really start at the same moment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the two איסורים really begin together. It sets up a challenge from a משנה about a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say that both איסורים come at the same time? But a משנה says: for these טומאות a נזיר shaves: for a dead body, and for a כזית from a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the other half of Step 11, the claim that both איסורים start together. It quotes a משנה about a נזיר. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if גיד הנשה applies to a non-kosher fetus, the two איסורים might not start at the same moment. The משנה about a נזיר is the first piece of evidence. Its point only becomes clear once the next step explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Together, at the same time
A person who took a vow not to drink wine, cut his hair, or become טמא from a dead body
Shaves (a נזיר who became טמא from a dead body shaves and starts his נזירות again)
An olive's size, the minimum amount for many laws

phrases.english: And can you really say
that both of them come at the same time?
phrases.notes: "Both" means the גיד הנשה איסור and the non-kosher איסור.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
For these impurities a נזיר shaves:

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַמֵּת וְעַל כְּזַיִת מִן הַמֵּת.
phrases.english: for a dead body, and for an olive's size of a dead body.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתוּ? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second attack on Step 11, now on its timing claim
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the גיד הנשה איסור and the non-kosher איסור start together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה, as explained in the next step, will show that a fetus's limbs exist before its sinews, so the two איסורים cannot start together

steps.title: A fetus has limbs before sinews, so the non-kosher איסור comes first
steps.stepSummary: Through רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה, the גמרא proves that limbs form before sinews. So the non-kosher איסור starts first.
steps.simpleTranslation: We had a difficulty: if a נזיר shaves for a כזית of a dead body, surely he shaves for a whole body! רבי יוחנן said the case is needed only for a miscarried fetus whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews. So we see the non-kosher איסור comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה through רבי יוחנן. From that explanation it concludes that the non-kosher איסור begins before the גיד הנשה איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing "a whole body" seemed pointless, because a כזית is already enough. רבי יוחנן says it teaches about a tiny fetus with limbs but no sinews yet, which still counts as a whole body. So a fetus has flesh before it has sinews. The flesh is already forbidden as non-kosher before the גיד exists, so the two איסורים do not start together.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so, obviously
It is needed only for... (points to the specific case a rule is teaching)
A miscarried fetus
Sinews, nerves
Evidently, so we see
Comes first, takes effect earlier

steps.confusionAlert: In the last line, אִיסּוּר טוּמְאָה does not mean ritual impurity. It means the איסור of a non-kosher (טמאה) animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks out the answer of Step 11. Now the non-kosher איסור is already in place when the גיד forms, so the question returns: how can רבי יהודה make a person liable twice?

phrases.english: And it was difficult for us:
If he shaves for an olive's size of a dead body,

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַמֵּת כּוּלּוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then for a whole dead body, isn't it all the more so?
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is needed only for a miscarried fetus
whose limbs have not yet been joined by sinews.
phrases.notes: Such a tiny fetus has less than a כזית, but as a whole body it still makes the נזיר shave.

phrases.english: So we see the non-kosher איסור comes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה from Step 14 and finishes the challenge
steps.raayaObject: That the non-kosher איסור takes effect before the גיד הנשה איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a נזיר, together with רבי יוחנן's explanation about a נפל whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews

steps.title: The nerve prohibition still takes effect because it applies to בני נח
steps.stepSummary: Even though the non-kosher איסור comes first, the גיד הנשה איסור still takes effect on top of it, because the nerve איסור also applies to בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the non-kosher prohibition comes first, the nerve prohibition comes and takes effect on it anyway, since the nerve prohibition applies to בני נח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 15. It admits that the non-kosher איסור starts first, but explains why the nerve איסור can still take effect on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a second איסור cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden. But the גיד הנשה איסור covers more people: it applies even to בני נח, while the non-kosher איסור does not. Because it adds something new, it is strong enough to take effect anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of eating a non-kosher (טמא) animal
Comes first, takes effect earlier
Takes effect on it (on something already forbidden)
Descendants of Noah: people bound only by the seven Noahide laws

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the reasoning for רבי יהודה's view that someone gets two sets of מלקות for eating the nerve of a non-kosher animal.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the nerve איסור came first. It agrees that the non-kosher איסור came first, and explains why the nerve איסור takes effect anyway.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּר טוּמְאָה קָדֵים,
phrases.english: Even though the non-kosher prohibition comes first,
the nerve prohibition comes and takes effect on it,
since its prohibition applies to the descendants of Noah.
phrases.notes: בני יעקב kept the nerve איסור before מתן תורה, when they still counted as בני נח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף על גב דאיסור טומאה קדים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Steps 14-15, that the non-kosher איסור begins before the nerve איסור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning: the second איסור takes effect because it is broader in scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the non-kosher איסור starts first, the nerve איסור should not be able to take effect, so there should be only one punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nerve איסור takes effect anyway because it also applies to בני נח, which makes it broader than the non-kosher איסור.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's wording supports the בני נח reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יהודה's own words in the משנה point to this reasoning: the nerve was forbidden to בני יעקב while non-kosher animals were still permitted to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording supports this, since it teaches: רבי יהודה said: Wasn't גיד הנשה forbidden starting from בני יעקב, while a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer in Step 16 from the exact words of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה stresses that the nerve was forbidden to בני יעקב at a time when non-kosher animals were still allowed. That is the same point as Step 16: the nerve איסור reaches further than the non-kosher איסור, so it can take effect on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording also shows this; a support taken from exact wording
The sons of Jacob, before the Torah was given
A non-kosher animal
The sciatic nerve, forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the nerve איסור is older and wider than the non-kosher איסור, and that is why it can take effect on a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: This is also precise, since it teaches:
Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב נֶאֱסַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה,
phrases.english: Wasn't the sciatic nerve forbidden starting from the sons of Jacob,
while a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 16 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the nerve איסור takes effect on a non-kosher animal because it applied even before the Torah, to בני נח
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה that the nerve was forbidden to בני יעקב while non-kosher animals were still permitted

steps.title: Returning to the ברייתא: רבי יהודה gives two punishments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא quoted earlier and begins studying it: according to רבי יהודה, someone who eats the nerve of a non-kosher animal is liable twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: One who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal: רבי יהודה makes him liable for two,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a fresh look at the ברייתא it quoted earlier. It starts quoting it again so it can go through it line by line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the ברייתא was used as a source for other questions. Now, with the word גופא, the גמרא returns to examine the ברייתא on its own. The first line is רבי יהודה's ruling of two punishments: one for the nerve and one for non-kosher meat.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: returning to study a source quoted earlier
Makes him liable twice (two sets of מלקות)

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the ברייתא it quoted earlier, to look at it closely.

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹכֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה –
phrases.english: One who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal:
Rabbi Yehuda makes him liable for two,
phrases.notes: Two sets of lashes: one for the nerve and one for non-kosher meat. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: גופא האוכל גיד הנשה של בהמה טמאה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion and opens a new section that studies the ברייתא directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, one who eats the גיד הנשה of a non-kosher animal is liable for two sets of מלקות.
